Lot Dekkhang (Y58)

Region (English scoring-table grouping): Haless.

In one sentence: Turn an arena of mercenary nobles into a state apparatus, unite Bomdan with mercenaries, subjects, and a multi-ethnic army, then let an exiled hobgoblin challenge the Command if the conditions are met.

Story: Medium-high | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (38 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: local Mod supports EU4 v1.37.5.0; exact rework date unverified | Uniqueness: High | Tedium: Medium (mercenary and subject requirements) | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: High

The Origins of a Mercenary Kingdom

Lot Dekkhang already exists in 1444 as a kingdom in Bomdan, with its capital at Lapnam Amrik. The history script gives it a monarchy, Teplin culture, High Philosophy, and its unique Teplinbasiet Arena Kingdom reform; the ruler recorded in 1428 is Metnikhren. Neighbouring Bim Lau is marked as a historical rival. These are opening facts, not evidence that the player has already completed the later missions to unite Bomdan. [Local history script]

The offline English Wiki's country page is very short: it identifies a mercenary kingdom in Bomdan and gives its capital. The related arena page explains what makes the country distinctive: the arena, converted from an old High Temple, hosted duels, contests, and succession bouts for generations, while mercenary captains became noble Daulophs. Mission text adds that these military nobles are not ordinary feudal knights: state power is reorganized around the arena, the mercenary market, and their interests. Lot Dekkhang's central question is therefore not the destiny of one ruler, but whether an army can become a governable social institution. [Wiki] [Local narrative text]

From Border Kingdom to Bomdan Hegemon

The mission tree first addresses the surrounding states: draw Khao Elnak into the fold and restore it, unify the Thidinkai, and secure the Wulin frontier before advancing east. Another strand uses espionage and diplomacy against Bim Lau, seizes its tombs, and then claims the ability to protect the Rannir. Continued expansion leads toward Bomdan's cultures and porcelain cities. The “Bomdan Empire” in the missions is a political objective for the player to achieve, not the 1444 country name; no evidence establishes that this step requires changing Tag. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

Expansion is not powered only by the country's own levies. Dedicated missions combine subject administration, mercenary companies, and the military nobility: neighbouring peoples may be ruled through subjects, while others become sources of manpower or markets. The slums of Lapnam Amrik shift the story from foreign wars to domestic affairs. Human, Harimari, and hobgoblin gangs exploit local artisans and merchants; missions call for better roads, a secure market, action against the gangs, and the incorporation of some hobgoblin fighters into regulated mercenary service. Lot Dekkhang's most distinctive play is turning mercenaries from a temporary army into an entire system of public order, class, and finance. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

The late-game Command route has strict requirements: the ruler must belong to the Swallow Hobgoblin culture, follow Atheism, and employ a specified mercenary company to complete the mission “The Fourth Command.” If the target still exists, the script grants a Restoration of Union casus belli against the Command or a relevant successor; it does not automatically annex them or guarantee victory. This lets the player turn the hobgoblin refugee and mercenary story into a reversal of imperial ambition, but it is not an inevitable endpoint if the conditions are unmet. [Local script]

Practical Feel and Risks

At the start, establish a sustainable military base through the arena and mercenary nobles, then decide how to use subjects and hired troops to unite nearby peoples. Espionage against Bim Lau, defenses along the northern river, and later urban reforms make the campaign alternate between conquest and administration. The missions deal with religious and cultural difference, but “uniting Bomdan” is not itself equivalent to evil; the more relevant questions are whether residents receive meaningful protection and whether the army is wholly captured by noble interests. [Local script]

An early official Reddit roadmap described Lot Dekkhang as a “mercenary nobility” project. This documents the design direction at that time; it does not verify any present-day mission reward. Two player discussions praise combinations of mercenary cost and discipline, and the late-game objective of challenging the Command. These experiences depend on the version, reforms, and player choices, so their figures should not be carried over as current facts. A 2026 regional discussion also considers Lot Dekkhang's story insufficiently polished; strong mechanics do not mean the narrative has no shortcomings. [Official development roadmap] [Community opinion]

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 86/100 | Autocracy 68/100 | Magic–Artifice 55/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 21/100) | Pluralism 73/100. The magic–artifice direction has low thematic intensity and should carry little matching weight.

The v2.1 value profile is Neutral (64/100), with a branch-dependent trajectory. Reforming the slums, securing markets, and fielding a multi-ethnic army provide concrete public benefits; the missions also center military nobles, subject rule, and a conditional bid for hegemony. Conquest and monarchy do not lower the score by themselves. Treatment of residents across the full route has not been established, so the assessment remains neutral. Suitable for players who enjoy mercenary economics, military-political classes, and expansion on several fronts; avoid it if you dislike mercenaries and subjects or want an endgame objective without ruler-culture and religion requirements. [Local script] [Local narrative text]

See the evidence record for source locations, Wiki page scope, and unresolved points.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Lot Dekkhang (Y58) — Dekkhangi Ideas

Set ID: Y58_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Y58
    }

Dekkhangi Traditions

  • Caravan power: +20% (caravan_power; raw value 0.2).

  • Mercenary Discipline: +5% (mercenary_discipline; raw value 0.05).

1. The Dauloph System

Centred around the Dekkhang feudal contract, the mercenary nobility of Lot Dekkhang enjoy privileges not seen in other kingdoms, such as reduced taxes and levies. These mercenary nobles, called Daulophs, traditionally use these excess men and gold for investments into mercenary companies. For us, we benefit from having a larger mass of ready mercenaries, as well as capable men to lead them.

  • Mercenary manpower: +20% (mercenary_manpower; raw value 0.2).

  • General cost: -10% (leader_cost; raw value -0.1).

2. Teplinbasiet

Located on the highest hill of the city, the Teplinbasiet stands tallest amongst our city. One of the High Temples sought after by Harimar, the tigerfolk would conquer Lapnam Amrik, repressing and subjugating the populace under a zealous religious governor. Now under human jurisdiction, the temple has been subverted, with its conversion to a theatre and arena - the former teaching old folktales, and the latter showcasing combat prowess.

  • army_tradition_decay: -0.01 (army_tradition_decay; raw value -0.01).

3. Mercenary Dialect

Composed of many languages, Mercenary Dialect was developed with the purpose of exchanging information with many foreign clientele. Even past their time as mercenaries, the Daulophs of Lot Dekkhang commonly use it to communicate with foreign dignitaries - or to bewilder them.

  • Improve relations: +10% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Power projection from insults: +0.5 (power_projection_from_insults; raw value 0.5).

4. Weapon Market Bookkeeping

In the early 16th century, the Great Weapon Market at Lapnam Amrik had bloated to a massive size. Miles of stalls, violence between competing bands, and corrupt clerks undermined trade and the law. In 1546, Dimche Beokhting was appointed as manager of the market. She reorganised the stalls, settled disputes, hired diligent clerks, and created a new form of Bookkeeping named after her. The result was an efficient market, free of violence, and much more open for foreign trade than in centuries past.

  • Domestic trade power: +10% (global_own_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

5. Khram Ptaa National Academy

Established in 1597 by the famous veteran Tirakseb of the Grand Contingent, one of the most notorious High Philosophy academies in the world began following a disastrous defeat of the Grand Contingent. Originally military oriented, it expanded to host a wide variety of subjects, from Philosophy to Dekkhangi Literature. Now, there is a large surplus of scholars and academics whose ideas we can apply to the state.

  • Idea cost: -10% (idea_cost; raw value -0.1).

6. Sphangaokbrach Battery Tactics

In the last few centuries, cannons have become a common form of warfare in Haless. But the defensive infrastructure present in Bomdan needed special attention in order to be overcome. To this end, the development of the Sphangaokbrach "Copper Ram'' Batteries in 1680 gave Dekkhangi generals the ability to overcome the many forts found throughout Bomdan.

  • Artillery combat ability: +10% (artillery_power; raw value 0.1).

7. The Steel Constitution

Historically, the steel-bind contract, otherwise known as the Dekkhang, was a loose set of disjointed laws and firm privileges afforded to the Daulophs. This had always caused local officials to struggle with all the contradictory or vague laws that arose in the centuries after its establishment. Between 1732 and 1734, Metnikhren IV created a royal constitution, codifying the Dekkhang and adding new laws for the modern era, centralising the kingdom in the process.

  • global_autonomy: -0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).

  • Siege ability: +10% (siege_ability; raw value 0.1).
